alerts.description: V1 baseline: CommandLineEventConsumer triggered by __TimerEvent writes a marker once.

subscriptions.key: root\subscription::Windows Update Monitor->Windows Update Monitor Consumer

filter.name: Windows Update Monitor
filter.query: SELECT * FROM __TimerEvent WHERE TimerID = 'WindowsUpdateTimer' AND NumEvents > 0

evidence.title: High-risk permanent consumer class
evidence.detail: CommandLineEventConsumer executes an action automatically when the filter fires; it is the preferred T1546.003 consumer type.

evidence.title: WmiPrvSE spawned a suspicious child process
evidence.detail: Consumer execution produced: cmd.exe /c echo NT230-D12-MARKER > "C:\Users\Public\nt230_d12_marker.txt"

evidence.title: Command interpreter or LOLBin launch
evidence.detail: Action starts cmd.exe /c, which is typical for scripted execution but uncommon for monitoring consumers.

evidence.title: Name masquerades as a trusted component
evidence.detail: Subscription name contains 'Windows Update', a common masquerading pattern for T1546.003.

evidence.title: User-writable target path
evidence.detail: Action references %PUBLIC%, a location writable by non-privileged users (staging/marker location).

evidence.title: Subscription created by a non-SYSTEM principal
evidence.detail: CreatorSID S-1-5-21-1004336348-1177238915-682003330-1001 (NT230LAB\student) is not LOCAL SYSTEM; WMI persistence is normally installed by an interactive user or attacker context.

evidence.title: Activation logged under a user account
evidence.detail: Event 5861 for 'Windows Update Monitor' records user 'NT230LAB\student' rather than SYSTEM.

alerts.description: V2 filter + name variation: process-creation WQL (WITHIN 5) and a masqueraded ActiveScript consumer.

subscriptions.key: root\subscription::SCM Event Log Filter->SCM Event Log Consumer

filter.name: SCM Event Log Filter
filter.query: SELECT * FROM __InstanceCreationEvent WITHIN 5 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_Process' AND TargetInstance.Name = 'notepad.exe'

properties.ScriptText:
Set fso = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
Set f = fso.CreateTextFile("C:\Users\Public\nt230_d12_marker.txt", True)
f.WriteLine "NT230-D12-MARKER"
f.Close

evidence.detail: Inline script uses Scripting.FileSystemObject to create processes or write files, the usual ActiveScriptEventConsumer payload.
